about: Tool Rosetta: one idea, shown in every tool. Rendered by assets/js/tool-rosetta.js. Cells are short strings; `backticks` become code. Keep entries neutral and checkable against each tool's own docs.

course.name: This course
course.kind: The plain JavaScript you write in our lessons (Pixel Courier, Tiny-Loop)

r2d.name: Rosetta 2D
r2d.kind: Our own lightweight 2D engine (about 10 KB gzipped)

unreal.name: Unreal Engine 5
unreal.cost: Free to learn; royalties on big sales

gltf.name: .glb file
gltf.kind: What actually travels to the game engine

photopea.name: Photopea
photopea.cost: Free in the browser (ads); paid ad-free
photopea.kind: Photoshop-style editor in a browser tab

aseprite.name: Aseprite
aseprite.cost: Paid, or free to compile from source

png.name: .png file
png.kind: What actually travels to the game engine

concepts.what: The language you write game logic in.

cells.unreal: C++, or Blueprints (visual nodes)

concepts.what: Where the objects of one level or screen live.

cells.course: arrays of plain objects inside a `world`
cells.r2d: a `Scene`: a tree of Nodes; `scene.toJSON()` saves it
cells.godot: a Scene: a tree of Nodes, saved as `.tscn`
cells.unity: a Scene: GameObjects listed in the Hierarchy
cells.unreal: a Level: Actors listed in the Outliner
cells.gamemaker: a Room: instances placed on layers

concepts.what: How code gets attached to a thing in the world.

cells.course: functions that read and change the object
cells.godot: attach one script to a Node; add child Nodes for parts
cells.unity: add Components (your `MonoBehaviour` scripts) to a GameObject
cells.unreal: add Components to an Actor; logic in C++ or its Blueprint
cells.gamemaker: fill in Events (Create, Step, Draw…) on an Object
cells.phaser: methods on a class, or code in the Scene

concepts.what: Build an enemy once, place it many times.

cells.godot: save a branch as its own scene, then instance it
cells.unreal: a Blueprint Class
cells.gamemaker: an Object asset (each copy is an instance)

concepts.what: Setup code that runs when an object or level begins.

cells.course: an `init()` call before the loop starts
cells.unreal: `BeginPlay()` / Event BeginPlay

concepts.what: Create a new copy while the game runs.

cells.unreal: `SpawnActor` / Spawn Actor from Class node

concepts.what: Take something out of the game safely.

cells.course: mark `dead = true`, then filter the array
cells.r2d: `destroy()` (removed at the end of the step)
cells.unreal: `Destroy()` / DestroyActor node

concepts.gotcha: Most engines remove the object at the end of the frame, not instantly, so code later in the same frame can still see it.

concepts.what: Ask whether a button is held right now.

cells.unreal: Enhanced Input: an Input Action in a Mapping Context

concepts.gotcha: Name actions ("jump") instead of keys (Space). Then gamepads and remapping are free in Godot, Unity and Unreal.

concepts.what: One object says “delivered!” and others react, without knowing each other.

cells.unreal: an Event Dispatcher (a delegate)
cells.gamemaker: call a method on the other instance, or `event_user(0)`

concepts.what: Which way is up, and how big is “1”?

cells.r2d: pixels, y grows downward; x, y is the centre
cells.godot: 2D: pixels, y down. 3D: Y up, 1 unit = 1 m
cells.unreal: Z up, 1 unit = 1 cm, left-handed

concepts.gotcha: A model that is 100× too big or lying on its back almost always means units or up-axis were not converted on import.

concepts.what: Get a model from your 3D app into the engine.

cells.course: `GLTFLoader` from our Three.js bundle loads a `.glb`
cells.r2d: 2D only; pair with our Three.js bundle for 3D
cells.godot: drop the `.glb` in the FileSystem dock; it imports as a scene
cells.unity: drag FBX into Assets; `.glb` needs the glTFast package
cells.unreal: Import FBX or glTF into the Content Browser

concepts.what: Get a PNG into the engine and tell it what kind of data it holds.

cells.course: `new THREE.TextureLoader().load('T_Brick_BaseColor.png')`; set `colorSpace` to sRGB for colour maps only
cells.godot: Drop the `.png` in the FileSystem dock; for a normal map set Import → Normal Map: Enable
cells.unity: Drag into Assets; for a normal map set Texture Type: Normal map
cells.unreal: Import into the Content Browser; normal maps need Compression: Normalmap (auto-set for `_N` names)
cells.gamemaker: Create a Sprite and load the PNG; tiling textures go in a Texture Group

concepts.gotcha: Colour maps are sRGB; roughness and normal maps are linear (non-colour) data. Importing a normal map as colour makes lighting look wrong.

concepts.what: Run a named clip (Idle, Walk) that came in with a rigged model.

cells.r2d: 2D only; pair with our Three.js bundle for 3D
cells.godot: `$AnimationPlayer.play("Walk")`; set loop mode in the import settings
cells.unreal: Animation Blueprint, or `PlayAnimation(WalkAnim, true)` on the Skeletal Mesh

concepts.what: Let players bump into the prop using a few boxes, not every bevel.

cells.course: a `THREE.Box3` around the prop and an overlap test
cells.godot: Mesh → Create Collision Shape, or add `-col` to the object name before import
cells.unreal: Static Mesh Editor → Collision → Add Box Simplified Collision, or `UCX_` meshes

concepts.idea: Update an asset after you re-export
concepts.what: Replace the file and keep the work you did inside the engine.

cells.course: reload the page; the loader reads the new file
cells.godot: overwrite the `.glb`; Godot reimports it. Keep engine edits in an inherited scene
cells.unity: overwrite the file; Unity reimports it. Keep edits on a prefab
cells.unreal: right-click the asset → Reimport

concepts.gotcha: Engine-side work (collision, scripts, materials) lives on a wrapper around the import, so a re-export never wipes it.

concepts.what: Show a picture you drew.

cells.unity: import the PNG as Texture Type: Sprite (2D and UI); it gets a SpriteRenderer
cells.unreal: import the PNG, then Sprite Actions → Create Sprite (Paper2D)

concepts.what: Stop pixel art from going blurry when scaled.

cells.godot: Project Settings → Rendering → Textures → Default Texture Filter: Nearest
cells.unity: texture Filter Mode: Point (no filter), Compression: None
cells.unreal: Sprite Actions → Apply Paper2D Texture Settings
cells.gamemaker: Game Options: untick “Interpolate colours between pixels”

concepts.what: Draw at a tiny resolution, then scale up by 2×, 3×, 4×.

cells.r2d: `width: 320, height: 180`; the canvas scales with CSS
cells.godot: Stretch mode viewport + integer scale mode
cells.unreal: orthographic camera sized to your pixel resolution
cells.gamemaker: viewport = camera size × 3 (Room → Viewports and Cameras)

concepts.what: Cut one image into equal frames.

cells.godot: AnimatedSprite2D → SpriteFrames → “Add frames from sprite sheet”
cells.unity: Sprite Mode: Multiple → Sprite Editor → Slice → Grid By Cell Size
cells.unreal: Sprite Actions → Extract Sprites (grid mode)
cells.gamemaker: Sprite Editor → Image → Convert to Frames

concepts.what: Name a list of frames and a speed.

cells.godot: SpriteFrames animation “run”, speed 10 FPS, loop on
cells.unity: an Animation Clip (drag the frames into the Scene), 10 samples per second
cells.unreal: a Flipbook asset, 10 frames per second
cells.gamemaker: the sprite's frames + playback speed 10 fps
cells.pygame: a list `run = [f0, f1, f2, f3]` plus an fps number

concepts.what: Switch the character to the “run” frames.

cells.unreal: `SetFlipbook(RunFlipbook)` on the flipbook component

concepts.what: Exactly one state (idle, run, jump…) at a time, with rules for switching.

cells.godot: AnimationTree with a state machine, or a `match state:` block
cells.unity: an Animator Controller: states + transitions on parameters
cells.unreal: an enum + `switch` in Tick (Paper2D has no animation graph)
cells.pygame: your own `if/elif`, or a dict of state functions

concepts.what: Show the frames for the current state without restarting them every frame.

cells.unreal: `SetFlipbook()` only when the state changes
cells.gamemaker: set `sprite_index` only when the state changes
cells.pygame: reset the frame timer only when the state changes

concepts.what: Mirror the sprite instead of drawing it twice.

cells.unreal: set the sprite's X scale to −1

concepts.what: What each tile looks like and whether it is solid.

cells.godot: TileSet resource with a Physics Layer per tile
cells.unity: Tile assets in a Tile Palette; solidity from each tile's Collider Type
cells.unreal: a Paper2D Tile Set with per-tile collision
cells.gamemaker: a Tile Set (tiles don't collide; use a collision tile layer or objects)

concepts.what: Place tiles on the grid.

cells.course: the level editor in the lesson
cells.unity: Grid + Tilemap, paint with the Tile Palette window
cells.unreal: a Paper2D Tile Map asset
cells.gamemaker: a Tile Layer in the Room editor
cells.phaser: `this.make.tilemap({ data, tileWidth: 16, tileHeight: 16 })` or a Tiled JSON map
cells.pygame: loop over the grid and `blit`, or load a Tiled map with pytmx

concepts.gotcha: The free Tiled editor saves maps that Godot, Unity, Phaser, GameMaker and Pygame can all load, so a level can move between engines.

concepts.what: Let each tile's neighbours choose its edge piece.

cells.r2d: not built in; use the bitmask code, or Tiled Terrain sets
cells.unreal: no built-in autotile; paint by hand or author in Tiled
cells.gamemaker: Tile Set → Auto Tiling (16- or 47-tile sets)
cells.phaser: done in Tiled with Terrain sets
cells.pygame: the bitmask code from the lesson

concepts.what: Run physics in equal time slices so a jump is the same height on every computer.

cells.godot: `_physics_process(delta)` runs at a fixed 60 Hz by default
cells.unreal: physics runs on its own; turn on Physics Substepping for steadier steps
cells.gamemaker: the Step event runs once per frame at the Game Speed (fixed by design)

concepts.what: Code that runs every frame, scaled by delta time.

cells.unreal: `Tick(float DeltaTime)` / Event Tick, in seconds

concepts.gotcha: Delta time comes in seconds, milliseconds or microseconds depending on the engine. Check before you multiply.

concepts.what: What is drawn on top of what.

cells.r2d: tree order, then `z`; `parallax: 0` for the HUD
cells.godot: node order + `z_index`; CanvasLayer for the HUD
cells.unity: Sorting Layer + Order in Layer; a Canvas for the HUD
cells.unreal: Translucency Sort Priority for sprites; UMG widgets for the HUD
cells.gamemaker: layer depth in the Room editor; Draw GUI event for the HUD
cells.pygame: the order you call `blit`; HUD last

concepts.what: Something with velocity that knows when it is on the ground.

cells.unity: Rigidbody2D: `rb.linearVelocity`; ground check with a short raycast
cells.unreal: Character Movement: `AddMovementInput()`, `IsMovingOnGround()`

concepts.what: Speed up downward a little every frame.

cells.unity: Rigidbody2D Gravity Scale (world value in Project Settings → Physics 2D)
cells.unreal: Character Movement → Gravity Scale

concepts.what: Forgive jumps pressed a moment too late or too early.

cells.unreal: two timers you write in Tick
cells.gamemaker: two timers you write in Step
cells.pygame: two timers you write in the loop

concepts.gotcha: No engine does this for you. Game feel is design work in every tool.

concepts.what: Did these two things touch? (pick-ups, hazards)

cells.unreal: `OnComponentBeginOverlap` (Generate Overlap Events on)

concepts.what: Stop at walls and floors instead of passing through.

cells.r2d: done for you: walls are tiles or `Body({ static: true })`
cells.unity: a Dynamic Rigidbody2D + Collider2D does it for you
cells.unreal: Character Movement sweeps and slides for you
cells.pygame: move on x, fix overlaps, then move on y (as in the lesson)

concepts.what: Jump up through it, land on top of it.

cells.unity: Platform Effector 2D with Use One Way
cells.unreal: your own rule: ignore the platform while moving up
cells.gamemaker: only collide when `vsp > 0` and you were above it
cells.pygame: only collide when falling and you were above it

concepts.what: Keep the player on screen as they move.

cells.godot: Camera2D as a child of the player
cells.unity: a Cinemachine Camera with Tracking Target = player
cells.unreal: Camera + Spring Arm components on the character
cells.gamemaker: Room → Viewports and Cameras → Object Following
cells.pygame: `cam_x = player.x - W / 2`, draw everything at `x - cam_x`

concepts.what: Let the player move a bit before the camera follows, then ease after them.

cells.unity: Cinemachine Position Composer: Dead Zone + Damping
cells.unreal: Spring Arm → Enable Camera Lag
cells.gamemaker: Object Following borders; smoothing you lerp yourself
cells.pygame: dead zone and lerp you write

concepts.what: Never show past the edge of the map.

cells.unreal: clamp the camera position in code
cells.gamemaker: a following view stops at the room edges

concepts.what: Far layers scroll slower than near ones.

cells.unity: a small script: layer x = camera x × factor
cells.unreal: move each layer by camera x × factor in Tick
cells.pygame: draw the layer at `x - cam_x * factor`

concepts.what: Move between title, play and win screens; freeze the game.

cells.unreal: Open Level, Set Game Paused

concepts.what: Keep progress after the game closes.

cells.unreal: a SaveGame object + Save Game to Slot

concepts.what: Turn the project into something other people can play.

cells.r2d: upload the folder; scenes export as JSON, maps as Tiled JSON
cells.unity: File → Build Profiles → Web, Windows or macOS
cells.unreal: Platforms → Package Project (no official web export)
cells.gamemaker: pick a target (Windows, macOS, GX.games, HTML5…) and build
cells.pygame: pygbag for the web, PyInstaller for desktop

concepts.what: The kind of 3D data the app is made for.

cells.maya: polygon meshes and NURBS surfaces
cells.tinkercad: simple solids and holes combined together
cells.gltf: triangle meshes only

concepts.gotcha: CAD apps (Fusion, Onshape) are built for manufacturing: exact sizes, no UVs or rigs. Use them for hard-surface props, then finish game assets in a mesh app.

concepts.what: Move your view around the model (default mouse controls).

cells.blender: middle-drag orbit · Shift+middle pan · wheel zoom
cells.maya: Alt+left orbit · Alt+middle pan · Alt+right zoom
cells.max: Alt+middle orbit · middle pan · wheel zoom
cells.fusion: Shift+middle orbit · middle pan · wheel zoom
cells.onshape: right-drag orbit · middle pan · wheel zoom
cells.sketchup: middle-drag orbit · Shift+middle pan · wheel zoom
cells.tinkercad: right-drag orbit · middle pan · wheel zoom
cells.gltf: n/a: the file stores no view

concepts.what: How big is “1”?

cells.maya: centimetres by default
cells.gltf: always metres

concepts.gotcha: Maya's centimetres are why a model can arrive 100× too big. Decide your scale first, and check the export's unit setting.

concepts.what: Which axis points to the sky.

cells.maya: Y up
cells.gltf: Y up; exporters convert for you

concepts.what: The three basic transforms.

cells.maya: W · E · R
cells.onshape: Transform feature, or drag the triad
cells.tinkercad: drag, arrow keys, and the rotate handles
cells.gltf: a node's translation, rotation and scale

concepts.what: Work on the parts of a shape instead of the whole object.

cells.blender: Tab into Edit Mode; 1 · 2 · 3 = vertex · edge · face
cells.maya: F9 · F10 · F11 = vertex · edge · face
cells.max: convert to Editable Poly; 1 · 2 · 4 = vertex · edge · polygon
cells.fusion: pick faces and edges as inputs to features
cells.onshape: pick faces and edges as inputs to features
cells.sketchup: always on: click edges and faces directly
cells.gltf: vertices and triangles

concepts.what: Pull a flat shape out into 3D.

cells.maya: Edit Mesh → Extrude (Ctrl+E)
cells.onshape: Extrude feature (Shift+E) on a sketch region
cells.tinkercad: no extrude; drag a shape's height handle
cells.gltf: result only

concepts.what: A linked copy (instance) changes when the original changes.

cells.maya: Ctrl+D copy · Duplicate Special → Instance
cells.fusion: Paste = linked component · Paste New = independent copy
cells.onshape: insert the same part many times in an Assembly
cells.sketchup: Make Component (G); its copies are linked
cells.gltf: two nodes can share one mesh

concepts.what: Repeat a piece in a row or circle.

cells.maya: Duplicate Special with a transform, or MASH
cells.sketchup: Move with Ctrl to copy, then type `5x`
cells.tinkercad: Duplicate and repeat (Ctrl+D repeats the last move)
cells.gltf: baked into separate pieces

concepts.what: Model one half, get the other half free.

cells.maya: Mesh → Mirror
cells.gltf: baked into the mesh

concepts.what: Combine two shapes, or cut one with another.

cells.maya: Mesh → Booleans → Union / Difference / Intersection
cells.tinkercad: make one shape a Hole, then Group
cells.gltf: result only

concepts.gotcha: Mesh booleans can leave messy triangles. Check topology before you UV or rig.

concepts.what: Change an early step without rebuilding everything.

cells.blender: the modifier stack (live until you Apply)
cells.maya: construction history (INPUTS in the Channel Box)
cells.max: the modifier stack (Collapse to bake it)
cells.sketchup: none; Undo, and keep parts in groups
cells.tinkercad: Ungroup gets the original shapes back
cells.gltf: none: export bakes every step

concepts.what: The point the object rotates around and snaps by.

cells.maya: hold D (or Insert) to move the pivot
cells.tinkercad: no pivot; use the Workplane tool
cells.gltf: the node's local origin, which the engine pivots around

concepts.what: Make the current size and rotation the new “zero”.

cells.maya: Modify → Freeze Transformations
cells.gltf: unapplied scale travels as the node's scale

concepts.gotcha: Unapplied scale is the classic cause of wrong collision shapes and stretched physics in the engine.

concepts.what: Whether a surface shades smoothly or shows its facets.

cells.maya: Mesh Display → Soften Edge / Harden Edge
cells.tinkercad: the Sides setting on round shapes
cells.gltf: a normal stored for every vertex

concepts.what: Flatten the surface so a 2D texture can wrap it.

cells.blender: mark seams, then U → Unwrap (or Smart UV Project)
cells.maya: UV Editor → Automatic, then Cut and Unfold
cells.gltf: a UV coordinate stored for every vertex

concepts.what: Connect colour, roughness and normal images the way game engines expect.

cells.blender: Shader Editor → Principled BSDF; roughness and normal images set to Non-Color; normal goes through a Normal Map node
cells.maya: Hypershade → Standard Surface; roughness and normal files set to Raw
cells.max: Physical Material, or the glTF Material for exact export
cells.fusion: Appearances (for renders, not exported as game materials)
cells.sketchup: Materials panel; PBR maps in recent versions
cells.gltf: metallic-roughness: base colour, roughness/metal, normal, occlusion, emissive

concepts.gotcha: Only image textures travel reliably. Procedural nodes must be baked to images before export.

concepts.what: Bones that bend a character's mesh.

cells.blender: Armature, then Ctrl+P → With Automatic Weights
cells.maya: Skeleton → Create Joints, then Skin → Bind Skin
cells.max: Bones, CAT or Biped + Skin modifier
cells.gltf: a skin with joints

concepts.idea: Edit the rest pose vs. test a pose
concepts.what: Move joints in the rest pose; rotate them in a test pose. Fixing placement by posing hides the problem.

cells.blender: Edit Mode on the armature changes the rest pose; Pose Mode tests it
cells.maya: Move joints before binding; Skin → Go to Bind Pose to return to rest
cells.max: Edit bones with the Skin modifier off; Biped/CAT use Figure Mode
cells.gltf: stores the rest pose as each joint's inverse bind matrix

concepts.what: Control how strongly each bone moves each vertex (0 = not at all, 1 = fully).

cells.blender: Weight Paint mode; Normalize All keeps totals at 1
cells.maya: Skin → Paint Skin Weights; Component Editor for exact values
cells.max: Skin modifier → Paint Weights or Weight Tool
cells.gltf: up to 4 joint weights per vertex in each set, adding up to 1

concepts.gotcha: Weights that don't add up to 1 make vertices stretch or lag. The Asset Bench finds and normalizes them.

concepts.what: Record a pose at a moment in time.

cells.maya: S
cells.gltf: animation channels for translation, rotation and scale

concepts.idea: Keep each animation as a named clip
concepts.what: Store Idle, Walk and Run separately so the engine can play each one by name.

cells.blender: Dope Sheet → Action Editor: name the Action, click the shield (fake user); push to NLA
cells.maya: Time Editor clips, or Game Exporter → Animation Clips
cells.max: FBX export → Animation → Takes, or the Game Exporter
cells.gltf: one named animation per clip

concepts.gotcha: Default names (Action, Take 001, mixamo.com) become the names your code has to type. Rename before export.

concepts.what: Shape the timing between keys: smooth ease, hard snap, or a held pose.

cells.maya: Windows → Animation Editors → Graph Editor
cells.gltf: each channel is LINEAR, STEP or CUBICSPLINE

concepts.what: Send the finished asset to Godot, Unity, Unreal or Three.js.

cells.blender: File → Export → glTF 2.0 (`.glb`); FBX also built in
cells.maya: FBX built in; glTF needs a plugin
cells.max: FBX built in; glTF built in since 3ds Max 2023
cells.fusion: Export as OBJ or FBX, then clean up in a mesh app
cells.onshape: Export as STL or OBJ, then clean up in a mesh app
cells.gltf: one file with meshes, materials, rigs and animations

concepts.gotcha: Pick `.glb` when you can: every engine on this site reads it, so your art isn't tied to one app or one engine.

concepts.idea: Bring a fixed file back in
concepts.what: Open the cleaned-up export (for example from the Asset Bench) back in your app.

cells.blender: File → Import → glTF 2.0 (`.glb`/`.gltf`); also FBX, OBJ, STL
cells.maya: File → Import for FBX and OBJ; `.glb` needs a glTF plugin
cells.max: File → Import for FBX and OBJ; glTF import is in recent versions
cells.fusion: Insert → Insert Mesh (`.obj` or `.stl`): a mesh body, not editable features
cells.onshape: Import `.obj` or `.stl` as a mesh reference to model around
cells.sketchup: File → Import (Pro); `.stl` needs the free STL extension
cells.gltf: keeps names, materials, rigs and clips through the round trip

concepts.gotcha: Importing a fixed export doesn't fix your source file. Make the same fix in the source too, or the next export brings the problem back.

concepts.what: The file that keeps every layer so you can change your mind later.

cells.png: Not a source file: one flat picture

concepts.gotcha: Keep the source and the export side by side. You fix mistakes in the source, then export again.

concepts.idea: Export a PNG for the game
concepts.what: Write the flat image that engines, websites and other apps read.

cells.photoshop: File → Export → Quick Export as PNG, or Export As…
cells.aseprite: File → Export As… (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S) → `.png`; Export Sprite Sheet for animation frames
cells.png: lossless, keeps transparency, opens in every engine

concepts.gotcha: Export PNG, not JPG, for game textures: JPG blurs edges and can't store transparency.

concepts.what: Hand a layered file to someone who uses a different app.

cells.photopea: Native `.psd`, so layers travel to Photoshop, GIMP and Krita
cells.gimp: File → Export As → `.psd` (most layers survive; some effects flatten)
cells.krita: File → Save As → `.psd` (paint layers, masks and blend modes survive)
cells.photoshop: `.psd` is the shared format most apps read
cells.aseprite: Layers export as separate PNGs or a sprite sheet; no PSD
cells.png: Flattens every layer into one picture

concepts.what: Paint on a fresh sheet without touching what's below.

cells.photopea: Layer → New → Layer, or the + button in the Layers panel
cells.krita: Insert key, or + in the Layers docker
cells.png: Layers are merged on export

concepts.what: Make a safe copy before a risky change.

cells.procreate: Swipe left on the layer → Duplicate
cells.png: Layers are merged on export

concepts.idea: Hide part of a layer without erasing
concepts.what: Paint black to hide and white to bring it back.

cells.photopea: Mask button at the bottom of the Layers panel
cells.photoshop: Add layer mask button in the Layers panel
cells.aseprite: No layer masks: use a selection and a separate layer
cells.png: Masks are applied (baked in) on export

concepts.gotcha: Masks are undo you can come back to tomorrow. Erasing is permanent once you save.

concepts.what: Multiply for shadows and grime, Screen or Add for glows, Overlay for contrast.

cells.photopea: Blend-mode menu at the top of the Layers panel
cells.gimp: Mode menu in the Layers dock
cells.krita: Blending-mode menu in the Layers docker
cells.photoshop: Blend-mode menu in the Layers panel
cells.procreate: Tap the N on the layer
cells.png: The blended result is baked in

concepts.what: Levels, Curves and Hue/Saturation that you can tweak later.

cells.gimp: Colors menu (Levels, Curves, Hue-Saturation); GIMP 3 keeps filters editable
cells.krita: Layer → New → Filter Layer, or a Filter Mask
cells.procreate: Adjustments (magic-wand icon) → Hue, Saturation, Brightness / Curves
cells.png: Adjustments are baked in

concepts.idea: Add an outline, glow or drop shadow
concepts.what: Effects that follow the layer's shape.

cells.gimp: Filters → Light and Shadow → Drop Shadow (editable in GIMP 3)
cells.procreate: No layer styles: duplicate the layer, recolour and blur it
cells.png: Effects are baked in

concepts.what: Grab an area of similar colour in one click.

cells.png: Selections aren't saved in a PNG; transparency is

concepts.what: Drop the selection so tools work everywhere again.

cells.png: — selections stay in the app

concepts.what: Swap selected and unselected areas.

cells.png: — selections stay in the app

concepts.gotcha: Ctrl+I means different things in different apps (invert colours vs. invert selection). Check the menu.

concepts.what: Remove a spot or seam by blending in nearby texture.

cells.krita: Smart Patch tool, or a Heal brush preset
cells.photoshop: Spot Healing Brush (J) or the Remove tool
cells.procreate: No healing brush: use Clone, or paint over
cells.png: The repair is baked in

concepts.idea: Clone from one area to another
concepts.what: Copy texture from a clean spot onto a damaged one.

cells.photopea: Clone Stamp (S); Alt-click to pick the source
cells.gimp: Clone tool (C); Ctrl-click to pick the source
cells.krita: Clone brush preset; Ctrl-click to pick the source
cells.photoshop: Clone Stamp (S); Alt-click to pick the source
cells.aseprite: None: copy and paste a selection
cells.png: The repair is baked in

concepts.what: Resize or turn the contents of a layer.

cells.aseprite: Select, then drag the handles; Edit → Rotate / Flip
cells.png: Transforms are baked in

concepts.what: Cut the picture down to the part you need.

cells.png: Stores only the final size

concepts.idea: Resize the image (power of two for games)
concepts.what: Change the pixel size. Game textures should be 256, 512, 1024 or 2048 px.

cells.krita: Image → Scale Image to New Size (Ctrl+Alt+I)
cells.procreate: Actions → Canvas → Crop & Resize (turn on Resample)
cells.aseprite: Sprite → Sprite Size (nearest-neighbour keeps pixels crisp)
cells.png: Any size, but engines compress and mipmap power-of-two sizes best

concepts.gotcha: Shrinking is safe. Enlarging only adds blur, never detail. For pixel art, use nearest-neighbour.

concepts.what: Type words onto the image.

cells.png: Text becomes pixels; keep the source to edit it

concepts.what: Step back through your changes.

cells.png: No history: export a new version instead of overwriting

concepts.what: Hide the seam so the texture can repeat across a floor or wall.

cells.photopea: Filter → Other → Offset by half the width and height (wrap around), then heal the seams
cells.gimp: Layer → Transform → Offset (Shift+Ctrl+O), by half; or Filters → Map → Tile Seamless
cells.krita: View → Wrap Around Mode (W): paint across the edges live
cells.photoshop: Filter → Other → Offset by half (Wrap Around), then heal the seams
cells.procreate: No wrap mode: move a copy by half with Snapping on, then paint over the seam
cells.aseprite: View → Tiled Mode → Tiled in both axes
cells.png: Tiling is a property of the pixels: if the edges match, it repeats

concepts.gotcha: Test it 3×3 before calling it done. A seamless edge can still show a repeating blotch.

concepts.what: Fake small bumps and dents from a grey height image.

cells.photopea: No built-in normal-map filter: use the Asset Bench or a dedicated texture tool
cells.krita: Filter → Edge Detection → Height to Normal Map
cells.photoshop: No current filter (the old 3D menu was removed); use the Asset Bench or Substance
cells.procreate: No normal-map tool: export the colour PNG and use the Asset Bench
cells.aseprite: Usually hand-painted for pixel art, or generated by the Asset Bench
cells.png: Store as non-colour (linear) data; Unreal flips the green channel

concepts.gotcha: Godot, Unity, Blender and glTF read OpenGL normals (green up). Unreal reads DirectX (green down). Mark the image as a normal map when you import it.
